pages.x: In 1494 the young king of France, Charles VIII, crossed the Alps with an army of 25,000 and a train of new bronze cannon, to claim the kingdom of Naples. The Italian states, used to small wars fought by hired captains, could not stop him, and he rode into Naples in February 1495.

His cannon smashed in hours walls that had held out for months. Italy became the training ground of Europe: Swiss pikemen, Spanish soldiers with arquebuses, German landsknechts in slashed and puffed clothes, and new star-shaped forts built to stand up to cannon fire.

Watching the chaos as a diplomat of Florence, Niccolò Machiavelli wrote The Prince, a handbook on how a ruler wins and keeps power, by force and cunning if need be. He held up as a model Cesare Borgia, the pope's son, who had carved out a state for himself in these wars.

The French king Francis I won a great victory at Marignano in 1515. But at Pavia in 1525 the army of the emperor Charles V, who was also king of Spain, cut down his knights with arquebus fire, and Francis was taken prisoner. He wrote to his mother that all was lost except his honour and his life.

In May 1527 Charles's unpaid army, many of them German Lutherans, mutinied and stormed Rome. For months they looted, tortured and killed. The pope's Swiss Guards held the steps of St Peter's long enough for Clement VII to flee to his castle; new guards still swear their oath on that day, 6 May.
pages.of: of 189 Swiss Guards died saving the pope

pages.x: The wars dragged on, with France even allying with the Ottoman Turks. In 1559 France and Spain made peace at Cateau-Cambrésis, leaving Spain master of Milan, Naples and Sicily. At a tournament held to celebrate, a splinter from a lance pierced the eye of the French king, Henry II, and he died.

The wars left Spain master of Italy for 150 years, and taught Europe a new way of war. They also spread the Renaissance: kings who came to fight went home with Italian painters, builders and ideas. Francis I brought Leonardo da Vinci to France, where he died.
pts: France and Spain fought over Italy for 65 years
Spain won Milan, Naples and Sicily
